This is a standard FHIR operation that returns a Bundle containing all resources in the Patient Compartment for a given patient, plus referenced resources (Organizations, Practitioners, PractitionerRoles, Locations, Medications, Devices).\n   104→\n   105→The export is invoked via:\n   106→```\n   107→GET [base]/R4/Patient/<id>/$everything\n   108→```\n   109→\n   110→The output is a **FHIR R4 JSON Bundle** — the documentation explicitly states this is \"the supported machine readable Electronic Health Information Export (EHI) format for Medplum.\"\n   111→\n   112→### What the Export Includes\n   113→\n   114→The export returns all resources in the FHIR R4 Patient Compartment. Based on analysis of the source code (`patienteverything.ts`) and the CapabilityStatement, this includes **68 resource types** that can be linked to a patient:\n   115→\n   116→**Clinical data resources:**\n   117→- Patient demographics\n   118→- AllergyIntolerance, Condition (diagnoses/problems)\n   119→- Observation (vitals, labs, clinical observations)\n   120→- DiagnosticReport (lab (Alternative Mechanism)\n   160→\n   161→Medplum also supports the FHIR Bulk Data API 2.0.0 (`/fhir/R4/$export` and `/fhir/R4/Group/<id>/$export`), which exports data in NDJSON format. While not explicitly designated as the b(10) mechanism (that's `$patient-everything`), the system-level `$export` can export all FHIR resources in a Project, which is effectively a superset. The Bulk FHIR API page includes complete Python code examples for performing the export.\n   162→\n   163→### Data Dictionary\n   164→\n   165→Medplum's data dictionary is the FHIR R4 specification itself. Because Medplum is \"FHIR-native\" (it stores data in FHIR format), the schema for every resource type is the standard FHIR R4 schema plus any Medplum-specific extensions. Unlike traditional EHRs where the export might only cover a subset of the internal data model, Medplum's export mechanism returns everything in the Patient Compartment because the Patient Compartment IS the internal storage model. This is a fundamental architectural advantage for EHI completeness.\n   178→\n   179→**Clearly covered domains:**\n   180→- Demographics (Patient resource)\n   181→- Diagnoses/problems (Condition)\n   182→- Medications (MedicationRequest, MedicationAdministration, MedicationDispense, MedicationStatement)\n   183→- Lab results/observations (Observation, DiagnosticReport)\n   184→- Vital signs (Observation)\n   185→- Allergies (AllergyIntolerance)\n   186→- Immunizations (Immunization)\n   187→- Procedures (Procedure)\n   188→- Clinical notes (Composition, DocumentReference)\n   189→- Care plans (CarePlan, Goal, CareTeam)\n   190→- Encounters/visits (Encounter, EpisodeOfCare)\n   191→- Family history (FamilyMemberHistory)\n   192→- Imaging (ImagingStudy, Media)\n   193→- Questionnaire/assessment responses (QuestionnaireResponse)\n   194→- Insurance/coverage (Coverage, CoverageEligibilityRequest/Response)\n   195→- Billing/claims (Claim, ClaimResponse, ExplanationOfBenefit, ChargeItem, Account, Invoice)\n   196→- Appointments/scheduling (Appointment, AppointmentResponse, Schedule)\n   197→- Communications (Communication, CommunicationRequest)\n   198→- Consent records (Consent)\n   199→- Documents and attachments (DocumentReference, Binary — though Binary is excluded from compartment search by default per the source code)\n   200→- Implantable devices (DeviceUseStatement, Device — resolved via references)\n   201→\n   202→**Key nuance — platform vs. product:**\n   203→Because Medplum is a platform (headless EHR), the actual data stored varies entirely by deployment. A pediatric telehealth deployment will have different resource types populated than a radiology deployment. The export mechanism is complete in the sense that it exports *everything the deployment has stored* for a patient, but what's stored depends on how the customer built their application.\n   204→\n   205→**Potential gap — Binary resources:**\n   206→The source code explicitly excludes `Binary` from compartment search (`r.code === 'Binary' ? undefined : r.code`). Binary resources hold raw file data (PDFs, images, DICOM). If clinical documents are stored as Binary + DocumentReference, the DocumentReference would be exported but the actual binary content might not be, depending on how references are resolved. This is a minor concern — the reference resolution code would include them if they're referenced by a resource in the compartment through one of the six allowed reference types, but it depends on the reference chain.\n   207→\n   208→**Not applicable (not a gap):**\n   209→- Specialty-specific clinical data: Medplum handles this through FHIR extensions and Questionnaire/QuestionnaireResponse, which are included in the export\n   210→- Custom assessments: Captured as QuestionnaireResponse, included\n   211→- E-prescribing data: Flows through DoseSpot integration but medication data stored in Medplum as MedicationRequest resources, included\n   212→\n   213→### Export Format & Standards\n   214→\n   215→- **Format**: FHIR R4 JSON Bundle (for `$patient-everything`); NDJSON (for Bulk FHIR API)\n   216→- **Standard**: HL7 FHIR R4 (4.0.1) — the recognized international standard for healthcare interoperability\n   217→- **Profiles**: The documentation references US Core STU 5.0.1 profiles (adopted via SVAP for g(10)), but the export is not limited to US Core resource types — it includes the full Patient Compartment\n   218→- **Schema**: Fully defined in the OpenAPI 3.1 spec (737 schemas) and CapabilityStatement (146 resource types)\n   219→\n   220→This is an appropriate format. Since Medplum's internal data model IS FHIR, the export is lossless — there is no transformation or lossy conversion from an internal format to the export format. A third party with FHIR knowledge could reconstruct the complete patient record from the exported Bundle.\n   221→\n   222→### Documentation Quality\n   223→\n   224→**Strengths:**\n   225→- Clear, developer-oriented documentation written for a technical audience\n   226→- The `$patient-everything` page is concise and actionable — it tells you the endpoint, parameters, and output format\n   227→- Complete machine-readable artifacts: CapabilityStatement (313 KB) and OpenAPI spec (2.6 MB) are publicly accessible without authentication\n   228→- Open source: the actual implementation is readable on GitHub, providing the ultimate source of truth\n   229→- Per-resource documentation pages with field definitions, data types, descriptions, search parameters, and links to US Core profiles\n   230→- Explicit statement connecting the operation to EHI/Cures Act compliance\n   231→- The ONC compliance page cleanly maps b(10) to the `$patient-everything` operation\n   232→\n   233→**Weaknesses:**\n   234→- No sample export output (a sample Bundle showing what a real `$patient-everything` response looks like would be helpful)\n   235→- No explicit enumeration of which resource types are in the Patient Compartment (the docs say \"FHIR R4 Patient Compartment\" and link to the FHIR spec, but don't list them on the page itself)\n   236→- No export instructions for non-developer users (the documentation assumes API literacy)\n   237→- The documentation doesn't discuss the Binary resource exclusion or its implications\n   238→- The Bulk FHIR API is documented separately but its relationship to b(10) vs g(10) could be clearer\n   239→\n   240→### Structure & Completeness\n   241→\n   242→- **Field-level granularity**: Excellent. The OpenAPI spec provides complete field definitions for every resource type including name, type, description, required/optional, and cardinality. The documentation pages add search parameters with FHIRPath expressions.\n   243→- **Value sets**: Referenced via the FHIR specification standard bindings. The ASC product is built on the gGastro platform, so both share the same underlying data model and export mechanism.\n\n**Export Format:** The export produces a package of CSV files, one per entity/table. Staff, locations, users, task management, audit logs, configurations\n- **Telehealth:** Telehealth session data\n- **Quality Reporting:** ASC quality measures, AGA registry data, GIQUIC registry data\n\n**Data Schema:** A complete relationship model showing how all 416 tables connect hierarchically through foreign key relationships, rooted at the Patient entity.\n\n**Translations/Value Sets:** Coded fields reference translation tables providing human-readable values for dozens of domains (billing codes, appointment statuses, procedure types, clinical scores, etc.). An additional 551-page supplementary document provides extended value sets including occupation codes.\n\n**Document Reconstruction:** Instructions explain how to reconstruct file paths for binary documents (PDFs, images) associated with services, imaging, portal uploads, statements, and letters.\n\n---\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage: STRONG\n\nThe ~416 CSV entities cover an exceptionally broad range of clinical, administrative, and financial data domains. The export goes well beyond USCDI minimum requirements to include:\n\n- Complete billing/claims data (30+ entities)\n- Specialty-specific clinical data (GI, ophthalmology, cardiology)\n- ASC-specific operational data (quality measures, anesthesia records)\n- Patient portal and engagement data\n- Scheduling and administrative data\n- Full document/attachment reconstruction support\n\nThis appears to export the **complete database schema** rather than a curated subset, which is the ideal approach for §170.315(b)(10) compliance.\n\n### Format & Standards: PROPRIETARY BUT WELL-DOCUMENTED\n\n- **CSV format** — widely readable by any spreadsheet or data tool, but not a healthcare-specific standard (not FHIR, C-CDA, etc.)\n- **Proprietary schema** — the entity names and field structures are Translation tables map codes to human-readable values\n- The export covers clinical, financial, operational, and engagement data\n\n### Overall Assessment\n\nModMed ASC provides **strong EHI export documentation**.
